arti_00001.name: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry

direct_claims.text: The Message Passing Neural Network (MPNN) achieves state‑of‑the‑art performance on all QM9 regression targets, reaching chemical accuracy on 11 of the 13 targets and outperforming prior models such as SchNet and DTNN.
Inference with the MPNN takes roughly 10⁻² seconds per molecule, about 300,000 times faster than the DFT reference calculation (~10³ seconds).
The multiple‑tower architecture reduces the computational complexity of a propagation step from O(n²d²) to O(n²d²/k) and yields a 2× speedup for n=9, d=200, k=8.
A general training method allows MPNNs to use larger node representation dimensions without increasing computation time or memory, providing substantial savings over previous high‑dimensional MPNNs.

arti_00002.name: SchNet: A continuous-filter convolutional neural network for modeling quantum interactions

direct_claims.text: Continuous-filter convolutional (cfconv) layers enable convolution on arbitrarily positioned inputs, overcoming the limitations of discrete filters that require grid-aligned data.
SchNet provides rotationally invariant energy predictions and rotationally equivariant, energy‑conserving force predictions by defining forces as the negative gradient of the predicted energy.

When trained on MD17 trajectories with a combined energy‑and‑force loss, SchNet achieves energy MAE ≤0.12 kcal/mol and force MAE ≤0.33 kcal/mol/Å, matching or surpassing GDML and DTNN on all tested molecules, including flexible ones such as malonaldehyde and ethanol.
Training SchNet with forces on only 1,000 examples yields better accuracy than training on 50,000 examples using energies alone, demonstrating that force information improves data efficiency.

arti_00003.name: Artificial Intelligence for Multiscale Modeling in Solid-State Physics and Chemistry: A Comprehensive Review

direct_claims.text: Artificial intelligence has transformed multiscale modeling by linking atomic, mesoscale, and continuum scales, delivering improved accuracy and reduced computational cost compared with traditional methods.

Machine‑learning‑driven interatomic potentials (e.g., GAP, DeePMD) and DFT‑trained surrogate models enable simulations of up to millions of atoms while retaining accuracy close to first‑principles benchmarks, making large‑scale high‑fidelity simulations feasible.

Neural‑network‑based electronic‑structure prediction tools achieve significant speedups over conventional density‑functional theory while maintaining comparable accuracy, accelerating electronic‑structure calculations.
Graph neural network architectures such as MEGNet and SchNet enhance prediction of phase transitions, defect dynamics, and bulk material properties relative to classical computational approaches.

other.text: Comprehensive review of AI-driven multiscale modeling approaches for solid‑state physics and chemistry

arti_00004.name: MACE: Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing Neural Networks for Fast and Accurate Force Fields

direct_claims.text: MACE uses four-body (higher-order) messages, allowing only two message‑passing layers to achieve converged accuracy, whereas prior equivariant MPNNs required five or six layers.
MACE attains state‑of‑the‑art accuracy, achieving lower root‑mean‑square energy and force errors than previous models on the rMD17, 3BPA, and AcAc benchmark suites.

MACE evaluates roughly ten times faster than prior force‑field models for invariant (L=0) architectures and 4–5 times faster for equivariant (L=1,2) architectures, while delivering lower prediction errors.

MACE shows superior extrapolation ability, reducing energy RMSE by about 30 % at 1200 K and 40 % on dihedral‑slice energies for the 3BPA benchmark, and achieving lower errors on geometries far from the training distribution.

arti_00005.name: General framework for E(3)-equivariant neural network representation of density functional theory Hamiltonian

direct_claims.text: DeepH-E3 provides a universal E(3)-equivariant deep-learning framework that exactly preserves Euclidean symmetry of the DFT Hamiltonian, including spin-orbit coupling.

DeepH-E3 predicts DFT Hamiltonian matrix elements with sub‑meV mean absolute error, reducing the error by roughly a factor of two compared with the original DeepH method across diverse material systems.

DeepH-E3 enables accurate electronic‑structure calculations for supercells larger than 10⁴ atoms, reducing computational cost by several orders of magnitude and allowing calculations in minutes on a single GPU versus months on thousands of CPU cores.

DeepH‑E3 reproduces the band structure of magic‑angle twisted bilayer graphene (θ = 1.08°, 11 164 atoms) in excellent agreement with DFT and low‑energy continuum models, correctly capturing the flat bands near the Fermi level.

arti_00006.name: Phonon predictions with E(3)-equivariant graph neural networks

direct_claims.text: Phonax efficiently predicts phonon dispersion relations and density of states for inorganic crystal materials.

Including Hessian (second‑derivative) data in training improves the energy model accuracy beyond training with only energy and force data, reduces force MAE, and provides an effective ~7× increase in the amount of force information.
Augmenting a minimal 1×1×1 supercell training set with Hessian data yields more accurate phonon predictions than training on a larger 3×3×3 supercell alone.
The E(3)-equivariant graph neural network architecture automatically preserves crystalline symmetries, yielding the correct acoustic‑sum‑rule zero modes without additional corrections.

arti_00007.name: GNN-Assisted Phase Space Integration with Application to Atomistics

direct_claims.text: Standard Gaussian quadrature rules produce frame‑dependent (non‑objective) phase‑averaged internal energies for rotated crystal lattices.
Gaussian quadrature leads to abrupt energy jumps and fictitious minima when neighbor cut‑off radii change during large deformations.
Third‑order Gaussian quadrature fails to approximate phase‑space integrals for bulk aluminum above 300 K, producing spurious minima in the Helmholtz free‑energy landscape.
Fifth‑order Gaussian quadrature yields internal energies and free‑energy curves that remain in good agreement with molecular dynamics results across the full temperature range studied.

arti_00008.name: Predicting ionic conductivity in solids from the machine-learned potential energy landscape

direct_claims.text: The frozen-framework PES descriptor screening ranks lithium-containing Materials Project compounds such that eight of the ten highest‑ranked materials are confirmed to be room‑temperature superionic conductors by first‑principles calculations.

The proposed screening method is approximately 50 × faster than molecular dynamics driven by a machine‑learning interatomic potential and at least 3 000 × faster than first‑principles molecular dynamics.

The combined descriptor Ξ, defined as the product of sigmoid‑transformed connected and disconnected free‑volume descriptors at a 0.5 eV threshold, achieves higher ranking scores than each individual descriptor and far exceeds random‑guess performance.

Free‑volume (FV) descriptors evaluated at energy thresholds between 0.3 eV and 0.5 eV consistently outperform or match the minimal percolation energy (MPE) descriptor across all three evaluation scores.

arti_00009.name: Machine Learning-Guided Discovery of Temperature-Induced Solid-Solid Phase Transitions in Inorganic Materials

direct_claims.text: A graph convolutional neural network predicts vibrational free energies with root‑mean‑square errors of 8.23 meV/atom (training), 11.34 meV/atom (validation) and 12.31 meV/atom (test), and its predictions for MgS and NaH polymorphs match DFT‑computed values across the 200–700 K range.

Screening of approximately 50 000 inorganic crystals with the machine‑learning model identified over 2 000 temperature‑induced solid‑solid polymorphic transitions between 300 K and 600 K, including 130 stable transitions within the technologically relevant 300 K–350 K interval.

Twenty‑one stable polar‑nonpolar transitions are predicted to exhibit relative lattice‑thermal‑conductivity changes of at least 20 % (0.20), ranging up to a 73 % increase for ZrSeO with a conductivity ratio of 1.73.

Several predicted solid‑solid transitions show large entropy changes exceeding 300 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹ (e.g., Li₃MnF₇: 342.3 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹, PnCl₂: 338.3 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹, Fe₄OF₇: 252.1 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹), while the highest entropy changes (> 400 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹) are limited to transitions above 450 K and occur exclusively in nonpolar‑nonpolar categories, reducing their relevance for room‑temperature applications.

other.text: Uncertainty-aware graph convolutional neural network for vibrational free‑energy prediction

arti_00010.name: Bridging scales with Machine Learning: From first principles statistical mechanics to continuum phase field computations to study order-disorder transitions in LixCoO2

direct_claims.text: A Hubbard U parameter of 2.5 eV in DFT+U (with a vdW‑DF exchange‑correlation functional) reproduces the experimental average lithiation voltages of LiCoO₂ across the composition ranges {0‑1}, {0‑0.5}, and {0.5‑1}.

A cluster expansion fitted to 333 DFT‑computed LiCoO₂ configurations using a genetic‑algorithm‑guided sparse regression achieves a root‑mean‑square error of 2.49 meV per primitive cell under 10‑fold cross‑validation and accurately reproduces formation energies, especially for configurations on or near the convex hull.
Large‑scale DFT calculations estimate the coherent anti‑phase boundary energy between the η₁ = ½ and η₃ = ½ ordered LiCoO₂ rotational variants to be 30.9 mJ m⁻².

Integrable Deep Neural Networks trained on derivative (chemical‑potential) data accurately learn the high‑dimensional free‑energy density and chemical‑potential functions for LiₓCoO₂, achieving mean‑squared errors comparable to the reported minima and reproducing DFT formation energies with a mean absolute error below 5 meV atom⁻¹.

other.text: Integrable Deep Neural Network (IDNN) for learning high‑dimensional free‑energy density and chemical potential functions

arti_00011.name: Matbench Discovery: A framework to evaluate machine learning crystal stability predictions

direct_claims.text: EquiformerV2+DeNS (a universal interatomic potential) achieves the highest classification performance among all evaluated models, with F1 scores up to 0.983, ROC AUC 0.96, and discovery acceleration factors up to 6.33, establishing state‑of‑the‑art for ML‑guided materials discovery.

Training universal interatomic potential models with forces, stresses, and magnetic moments substantially improves stability‑prediction performance compared with energy‑only models, enhancing both classification metrics (F1, DAF) and regression metrics (MAE, RMSE).

Regression‑based metrics such as MAE, RMSE, and R² are poorly aligned with classification‑based metrics needed for materials‑discovery tasks, and improvements in these regression metrics do not necessarily translate into higher F1 or discovery acceleration scores.

The WBM test set contains 215,488 unique prototype structures (32,942 thermodynamically stable), is enriched in actinides, lanthanides, metalloids and noble‑transition metals while under‑representing oxygen, is dominated by ternary phases (~75 %), and most structures have fewer than 100 atomic sites, contrasting with the Materials Project training distribution.

arti_00014.name: A Universal Graph Deep Learning Interatomic Potential for the Periodic Table

direct_claims.text: The final M3GNet interatomic potential achieves test mean absolute errors of 0.035 eV/atom for energy, 0.072 eV/Å for forces, and 0.41 GPa for stresses on a held‑out Materials Project dataset covering 89 elements.
Relaxing test crystals with M3GNet reduces median volume error from 2.4 % to 0.6 % and energy mean absolute error from 0.169 eV/atom to 0.035 eV/atom relative to DFT‑relaxed references.

A single‑CPU M3GNet relaxation completes in about 22 seconds, compared with 15 hours on 32 cores for DFT; pre‑relaxation with M3GNet shortens subsequent DFT relaxation time by roughly a factor of three and reduces total CPU time by an average factor of 2.97.

Screening 31.7 million hypothetical crystals with M3GNet identifies approximately 1.8 million candidates with predicted hull distances below 0.001 eV/atom, and among the 2,000 lowest‑energy candidates, 1,578 are confirmed stable (Ehull < 0.001 eV/atom) by DFT.

arti_00015.name: CHGNet: Pretrained universal neural network potential for charge-informed atomistic modeling

direct_claims.text: CHGNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Matbench Discovery benchmark, outperforming eight other submitted models.

On the Materials Project Trajectory test set, CHGNet trained with magnetic moment labels attains mean absolute errors of 30 meV/atom for energy, 77 meV/Å for forces, 0.348 GPa for stress, and 0.032 µB for magnetic moments.

CHGNet molecular dynamics simulations of Li superionic conductors reproduce room‑temperature ionic conductivities and activation energies within the error bars of AIMD, correctly distinguishing faster from slower conductors.
CHGNet integrates magnetic moment labels as a proxy for atomic charge, enabling inference of atomic charges and accurate differentiation of oxidation states such as V³⁺/V⁴⁺ and Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺.

arti_00016.name: Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics: a scalable model with the accuracy of quantum mechanics

direct_claims.text: DeePMD reproduces AIMD energies, forces, and virial tensors for water and ice with root‑mean‑square errors of approximately 1 meV per molecule for energy, 40 meV Å⁻¹ for forces, and 1–2 meV for the virial.
DeePMD accurately reproduces radial distribution functions and three‑body angular distribution functions of liquid water and ice, matching AIMD results.
For a diverse set of organic molecules, DeePMD achieves lower mean absolute errors in both energy and forces than the GDML benchmark.
The computational cost of DeePMD scales linearly with the number of atoms and is several orders of magnitude lower than equivalent AIMD simulations, comparable to empirical force fields.

Band structures and electric susceptibility computed from DeepH for MoS₂ match DFT results closely.

xDeepH accurately predicts the band structure of monolayer NiBr2 with a 19×1×1 spin‑spiral magnetic order, matching DFT results.
xDeepH generalizes to Moiré‑twisted bilayer CrI3 at a twist angle of 81.79°, a configuration not seen during training, reproducing band structures and density of states in agreement with DFT.

arti_00019.name: D4FT: A DEEP LEARNING APPROACH TO KOHN-SHAM DENSITY FUNCTIONAL THEORY

direct_claims.text: The QR‑based reparameterization used in D4FT preserves the orthonormal constraints of Kohn‑Sham orbitals, making the search space equivalent to the original orthogonal function space, as proved in Proposition 3.1, and can be interpreted as projected gradient descent on the orthogonal constraint set.

Direct minimization of the total KS‑DFT energy with stochastic gradient descent reduces the asymptotic computational complexity from O(N⁴) to O(N³), and the full‑batch D4FT algorithm has complexity O(nN²)+O(n²N²), which is lower than the O(n²N²) complexity of conventional SCF; minibatch training further lowers the cost.
D4FT converges to a self‑consistent Kohn‑Sham solution that satisfies the eigenfunction condition.
Across a benchmark set ranging from He to benzene, D4FT reproduces ground‑state energies of the reference PySCF implementation with deviations ≤0.02 Ha (LSDA/6‑31g and LSDA/STO‑3g).

arti_00020.name: Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Networks for an Accurate and Interpretable Prediction of Material Properties

direct_claims.text: The modified convolution function reduces the mean absolute error for formation‑energy prediction from 0.112 eV/atom to 0.039 eV/atom, achieving DFT‑level accuracy comparable to the experimental DFT‑experiment error of 0.081–0.136 eV/atom.
CGCNN classifies metals versus semiconductors with an area under the ROC curve of 0.95 and an overall accuracy of 0.90.

By extracting per‑atom site energies in perovskites, the model reveals that large‑radius elements stabilize the A site and group 4‑6 elements stabilize the B site, and using these insights the high‑throughput search space for stable perovskites is reduced by a factor of seven (from 18,928 to 228 candidates).

When applied to a set of 1,585 crystals with elastic properties, CGCNN predicts bulk modulus with a mean absolute error of 0.077 log(GPa) and shear modulus with a mean absolute error of 0.114 log(GPa), demonstrating good generalization.

arti_00021.name: Graph Networks as a Universal Machine Learning Framework for Molecules and Crystals

direct_claims.text: MEGNet models achieve lower mean absolute errors than SchNet on 11 of the 13 QM9 molecular properties evaluated.

Simple MEGNet models that use only atomic number and spatial distance as input achieve chemical accuracy, perform comparably to full‑feature models, and outperform prior state‑of‑the‑art models on 8 of the 13 QM9 properties.

MEGNet models trained on approximately 60,000 crystals outperform prior models (SchNet and CGCNN) for formation energy, band gap, bulk modulus, and shear modulus, achieving errors comparable to or better than density‑functional‑theory uncertainties.

A unified free‑energy MEGNet model that incorporates temperature, pressure, and entropy as global state inputs predicts U₀, U, H, and G with a combined mean absolute error of 0.010 eV, comparable to separate single‑property models.

arti_00022.name: Atomic cluster expansion of scalar, vectorial and tensorial properties and including magnetism and charge transfer

direct_claims.text: The atomic cluster expansion (ACE) is generalized to model scalar, vectorial and tensorial atomic properties and to include additional atomic degrees of freedom—species, magnetic moments, and charges—on equal footing with atomic positions.
The derived ACE formulas enable efficient evaluation of forces and magnetic torques.
At the lowest order, the magnetic ACE reproduces a distance‑dependent Heisenberg interaction.

Representing tensors with spherical harmonics yields a dramatically sparser basis, where a rank‑N Cartesian tensor with 3^N components can be represented by (N+1)^2 spherical harmonics (e.g., a 10th‑order tensor requires 121 harmonics instead of 59 049 Cartesian components).

DIRECT_CLAIMS: The atomic cluster expansion (ACE) is generalized to model scalar, vectorial and tensorial atomic properties and to include additional atomic degrees of freedom—species, magnetic moments, and charges—on equal footing with atomic positions.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: The derived ACE formulas enable efficient evaluation of forces and magnetic torques.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: At the lowest order, the magnetic ACE reproduces a distance‑dependent Heisenberg interaction.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: Representing tensors with spherical harmonics yields a dramatically sparser basis, where a rank‑N Cartesian tensor with 3^N components can be represented by (N+1)^2 spherical harmonics (e.g., a 10th‑order tensor requires 121 harmonics instead of 59 049 Cartesian components).
OTHER: Atomic Cluster Expansion extended to scalar, vectorial, tensorial properties with magnetic moments and charge transfer

arti_00023.name: Linking atomic structural defects to mesoscale properties in crystalline solids using graph neural networks

direct_claims.text: The GNN predicts atomic von Mises stress in polycrystalline graphene with a mean normalized relative error of 5.5% and a maximum error below 7% on a test set of 400 crystals.
The GNN predicts atomic tensile stress in porous graphene membranes under tensile strain with a mean normalized relative error of 4.9% and a maximum error of about 10%.
The GNN reproduces the linear decrease of Young’s modulus with vacancy concentration in porous graphene, matching MD results and yielding the fitted relation E = 823.7 − 5635.6·Cv (GPa).

In polycrystalline aluminum, the GNN predicts atomic potential energy with a mean normalized relative error of 11.0% (maximum ≈13%) and achieves R² = 0.99 for mean potential energy versus grain number.

arti_00024.name: The Joint Automated Repository for Various Integrated Simulations (JARVIS) for data-driven materials design

direct_claims.text: JARVIS-DFT contains approximately 40,000 materials and about 1 million calculated properties.
The integrated JARVIS workflow (DFT → FF → ML) enables rapid screening of materials for high solar‑cell efficiency (SLME) with predictions validated against experimental data.

Machine‑learning models trained on Classical Force‑field Inspired Descriptors (CFID) achieve high predictive accuracy for formation energies, exfoliation energies, band gaps, magnetic moments, refractive indices, dielectric constants, thermoelectric performance, and piezoelectric/infrared modes.
Using the vdW‑DF‑OptB88 functional for all dimensionalities yields accurate lattice parameters and formation energies for both van‑der‑Waals and non‑vdW bonded materials.

arti_00025.name: A Foundational Potential Energy Surface Dataset for Materials

direct_claims.text: UMLIPs trained on the MatPES dataset achieve test mean absolute errors in energies that are 4–10 times lower than UMLIPs trained on the larger MPRelax or OMat24 datasets.

Across equilibrium, near‑equilibrium, and molecular‑dynamics property benchmarks, MatPES‑trained UMLIPs match or surpass the performance of models trained on much larger datasets such as OMat24 (≈100 M structures).
Molecular‑dynamics simulations using MatPES‑trained UMLIPs exhibit markedly higher stability, with median termination temperatures up to ~1,900 K, versus ~1,300–1,500 K for MPRelax and OMat24 models.

On near‑equilibrium benchmarks, MatPES UMLIPs significantly improve the prediction of shear modulus (G_VRH) and off‑equilibrium forces while achieving similar bulk‑modulus (K_VRH) and heat‑capacity (C_V) accuracy compared to MPRelax and OMat24 models.

arti_00026.name: Materials Design and Discovery with High-Throughput Density Functional Theory: The Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD)

direct_claims.text: The Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD) contains over 200,000 DFT‑calculated crystal structures, including experimental ICSD entries and theoretical prototype structures, and is freely accessible to the scientific community without usage restrictions.
At 0 K and zero pressure, 23 % of the 32,489 ICSD structures in the OQMD are thermodynamically stable according to grand canonical linear programming analysis.
The average error between DFT‑predicted formation energies in the OQMD and experimental values from the SGTE database is 24 meV/atom, with a mean absolute error of 113 meV/atom.
High‑throughput screening identified TiP, LiSiNi₂, and CoSi₂ as the most promising Li‑ion battery anode conversion reactions, offering high capacity, moderate voltage, and low volume expansion.

arti_00027.name: AFLOW: an automatic framework for high-throughput materials discovery

direct_claims.text: AFLOW can automatically calculate a wide suite of physical observables across a large database of structures with minimal human intervention.

AFLOW detects most calculation failures, automatically corrects input parameters, restarts calculations, and can run as a Unix daemon to generate, run, correct, and converge many DFT jobs per day, yielding higher throughput than manual management.
AFLOW provides a standardized definition of Brillouin‑zone integration paths for all 14 Bravais lattices, filling a gap in the literature.
AFLOW reproduces experimental phonon dispersion curves for face‑centered cubic Rhodium, showing excellent agreement with measured data.

arti_00028.name: Machine learning a general purpose interatomic potential for silicon

direct_claims.text: The Gaussian Approximation Potential (GAP) for silicon reproduces density functional theory reference results across a wide range of observable properties, including bulk crystal, liquid, amorphous phases, and point, line, and plane defects.
For bulk elastic constants (B, C11, C12, C44) the GAP model achieves fractional errors of less than 10% relative to DFT, outperforming all other evaluated interatomic potentials.
Surface energies of the (111), (110) and (100) silicon cleavage planes are predicted by GAP with errors of around 2% relative to DFT, which is comparable or better than other potentials.
Formation energies of vacancy and interstitial point defects (hexagonal, tetrahedral, dumbbell) are predicted by GAP within 10% of DFT values, providing uniform accuracy across these defects.

arti_00029.name: Universal Machine Learning Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian for Materials

direct_claims.text: The universal HamGNN model achieves a mean absolute error of 5.4 meV for the real‑space Hamiltonian matrix on the test set after the first round of training.
Fine‑tuning the universal model on a small MOF dataset reduces the Hamiltonian matrix MAE to approximately 3.95 meV.

The universal HamGNN model accurately predicts the energy band structures and charge densities of complex multi‑element crystals (e.g., Hf2Zr9Ta6Ti5Nb5B54, HfTaTiB4MoC4, K3Ba3Li2Al4B6O20F), matching DFT results.
For the disordered solid‑electrolyte Li10Si1.5P1.5S11.5Cl0.5, the universal model predicts an insulating behavior with a band gap of 1.4 eV.

arti_00030.name: Using Deep Learning to Predict Fracture Patterns in Crystalline Solids

direct_claims.text: The ConvLSTM model accurately predicts fracture patterns, crack‑length trends, and both mode‑I (tensile) and mode‑II (shear) loading responses across crystal orientations, closely matching atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, with only a minor discrepancy for the x100 orientation under mode‑II shear.
The model predicts fracture toughness values that are comparable to those obtained from atomistic molecular dynamics simulations.

A model trained exclusively on single‑crystal data generalizes to bicrystal and gradient‑orientation crystals, reproducing MD fracture patterns for small orientation differences, capturing overall crack paths for large orientation differences, and handling arbitrary geometry gradients.
The ConvLSTM approach reduces computational cost dramatically compared with full molecular dynamics simulations, enabling rapid fracture predictions.

arti_00031.name: Flow Matching for Accelerated Simulation of Atomic Transport in Crystalline Materials

direct_claims.text: LiFlow predicts lithium mean‑squared displacement with a Spearman rank correlation of 0.7–0.8 on unseen material compositions, enabling screening of high‑diffusivity electrolytes.

LiFlow achieves speed‑ups of up to ~600,000× over ab initio molecular dynamics (and ~400× over MLIP), predicting a 1 ns trajectory in 48 s for a 2 × 2 × 1 LGPS supercell and 352 s for a 4 × 4 × 4 supercell.
The computational cost of LiFlow scales linearly with the number of atoms (O(n)), in contrast to the cubic scaling (O(n³)) of ab initio molecular dynamics.

Incorporating an adaptive, thermally and chemically conditioned Maxwell–Boltzmann prior markedly lowers mean absolute errors and raises rank correlations for MSD and RDF compared with an isotropic prior; ablation studies show performance degradation without it.

arti_00032.name: Commentary: The Materials Project: A materials genome approach to accelerating materials innovation

direct_claims.text: The Materials Project database contains computed structural, electronic, and energetic data for over 33,000 inorganic compounds, generated using more than 15 million CPU‑hours of computation.
The Materials Project provides an open RESTful API and a high‑level Python library (pymatgen) that enable programmatic querying and analysis of the full dataset.

The workflow software FireWorks together with the custodian job‑management tool automatically manages high‑throughput DFT calculations, self‑heals failed runs, and applies material‑type‑specific workflows.

Visual warnings are displayed on the Materials Project website for compounds whose calculated oxidation states, cell volumes, or bond lengths deviate significantly from experimental norms, helping users assess data reliability.

arti_00033.name: Simulating diffusion properties of solid-state electrolytes via a neural network potential: Performance and training scheme

direct_claims.text: The DeePMD model successfully reproduces the superionic behavior of solid-state electrolytes with linear Lithium/Sodium mean squared displacement over time and diffusion coefficient uncertainty of about 20% or smaller, which is precise enough for battery applications.
The DeePMD model provides excellent energy conservation in all tested systems up to 2 ns of NVE dynamics.
For LLZO, the computed activation energies range from 0.2 to 0.22 eV, in very good agreement with experimental values of 0.20-0.21 eV for cubic LLZO.
For LGPS, the computed activation energy is 0.16 eV, which is slightly lower than experimental values (0.22 eV) but in line with previous computational studies (0.17-0.21 eV).

other.text: DeePMD training protocol for diffusion coefficient computation

arti_00034.name: LEARNING INTER-ATOMIC POTENTIALS WITHOUT EXPLICIT EQUIVARIANCE

direct_claims.text: TransIP achieves SO(3) equivariance through training with a contrastive latent equivariance objective rather than hard-wired equivariant architectural constraints.
A generic unconstrained Transformer can serve as an effective backbone for machine-learned interatomic potentials without explicit equivariance constraints.
TransIP achieves 40% to 60% improvement in performance compared to data augmentation baseline (TransAug) across varying OMol25 dataset sizes.
In the limited data regime (1M samples), TransIP achieves 255 meV/Å force MAE versus 600 meV/Å for TransAug, with force cosine similarity of 0.7 versus 0.44.

arti_00035.name: Generalization of Long-Range Machine Learning Potentials in Complex Chemical Spaces

direct_claims.text: Long-range correction schemes in machine learning interatomic potentials are essential for achieving state-of-the-art accuracy, improving in-distribution performance, and enabling significant gains in transferability to unseen regions of chemical space.

Latent Ewald Summation cannot infer correct partial charges without reference charge labels and frequently predicts charges near zero or opposite in sign to reference values in challenging chemical environments such as MOFs.
CELLI-based models trained with reference charges consistently produce physically meaningful results and exhibit good performance across biased split benchmarks on MOF datasets.
Baseline versions of MACE and Allegro are degenerate with respect to total charge and cannot distinguish between molecules with different charge states without long-range corrections.

arti_00036.name: Scalable Parallel Algorithm for Graph Neural Network Interatomic Potentials in Molecular Dynamics Simulations

direct_claims.text: SevenNet achieves over 80% parallel efficiency in weak-scaling scenarios on a 32-GPU cluster with SiO2 benchmarks.
SevenNet-0 achieves mean absolute errors of 24 meV/atom for energy, 0.067 eV/Å for force, and 0.65 GPa for stress on the test set.
The parallelization algorithm restricts communication range between neighboring processors to the original cutoff radius (rc) rather than rc multiplied by message-passing steps.
Spatial decomposition is a valid parallelization strategy only if the energy can be decomposed into atomic energies, which is key for the linear scalability of GNN-IPs.

arti_00037.name: Pushing the limits of unconstrained machine-learned interatomic potentials

direct_claims.text: Unconstrained machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) trained on large datasets achieve accuracies on par with state-of-the-art equivariant architectures while maintaining orders-of-magnitude lower computational cost than quantum-mechanical methods.

The PET model achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on matbench-discovery benchmark (DAF=6.075, Accuracy=0.977, F1=0.924) and exceeds SOTA on SPICE molecular benchmark across most subsets for both energy and force predictions.
PET-OMAD demonstrates the best overall accuracy in predicting energies and forces on MADBench in almost all cases, with the highest success rate (98.43%) in predicting desorption reactions.

Fine-tuning models pre-trained on OMat24 to the MAD dataset achieves near-converged validation metrics in 30-100 epochs versus 700+ epochs when training from scratch, halving validation energy and force errors and achieving 50% lower test error than training on MAD alone.

arti_00038.name: Orb-v3: atomistic simulation at scale

direct_claims.text: Orb-v3 achieves near state-of-the-art performance across evaluations with at least 10x reduction in latency and 8x reduction in memory compared to alternative MLIPs.
Orb-v3-direct-20 uses only 32.8GB GPU memory for 100,000 atom systems and completes in under half a second, while all baseline methods and conservative models encounter Out Of Memory errors.
Orb-v3-direct-* models are the only universal MLIPs that can compute hundreds of forward passes per second, exceeding one million steps per hour for small systems.
Orb-v3-conservative-inf-omat achieves the highest accuracy for almost all physical property metrics while being faster than any best-performing model currently available in literature.

arti_00039.name: Open Materials 2024 (OMat24) Inorganic Materials Dataset and Models

direct_claims.text: OMat24 comprises over 118 million DFT calculations across diverse chemistries, materials, and configurations for inorganic bulk materials, making it up to 2 orders of magnitude larger than other openly available datasets in terms of number of single-point calculations.

OMat24 exhibits more uniform and comprehensive coverage of near-neighbor pairs and element distributions compared to both Alexandria and MPtrj datasets, with elemental coverage spanning most of the periodic table.

OMat24 contains a large fraction of far-from-equilibrium structures with 1 to 100 atoms per structure (majority having less than 20 atoms), yielding broader label distributions than relaxation-only datasets.

MLIP models trained on OMat24 achieve F1 scores above 0.9 for stability prediction and 20 meV/atom accuracy for formation energy on Matbench Discovery, with all five top-performing models on the Matbench Discovery leaderboard exclusively trained on OMat24.

arti_00040.name: UMA: A Family of Universal Models for Atoms

direct_claims.text: UMA models are trained on approximately 500 million unique 3D atomic structures (459M training examples with over 30 billion atoms) across five domains, representing the largest training runs to date for atomic models and covering nearly the entire chemical space except radioactive elements.

The Mixture of Linear Experts (MoLE) architecture enables increasing model capacity without sacrificing inference speed, with a compute-optimal MoLE model achieving equivalent validation loss to dense models using approximately 2.5× fewer active parameters.
UMA sets new state-of-the-art performance on Matbench Discovery and AdsorbML benchmarks, with UMA-M achieving the highest F1 score to date (0.929) on Matbench Discovery.
UMA-M reduces OC20 S2EF adsorption energy prediction errors by approximately 80% compared to previous state-of-the-art models, achieving 33.4 meV MAE versus 149.1 meV for EquiformerV2-OC20.

arti_00041.name: EQUIFORMERV2: IMPROVED EQUIVARIANT TRANSFORMER FOR SCALING TO HIGHER-DEGREE REPRESENTATIONS

direct_claims.text: EquiformerV2 outperforms state-of-the-art methods on OC20 and OC22 datasets, improving upon eSCN by 4-9% on force MAE and 4-18.9% on energy MAE.
EquiformerV2 trained on only OC22 (8.4M structures) achieves better results than GemNet-OC trained on both OC20 (130M structures) and OC22, demonstrating significantly better data efficiency.

EquiformerV2 can scale Lmax to 6 or 8 on OC20 dataset using eSCN convolutions that reduce computational cost from O(L^6) to O(L^3), whereas original Equiformer is impractical for Lmax > 2 on large-scale datasets.

EquiformerV2 offers better speed-accuracy trade-offs than Equiformer, being 2.3x faster at Lmax=2 while achieving better force MAE, and requiring 1.4x less training time when increasing Lmax from 2 to 4.

arti_00042.name: Benchmarking Materials Property Prediction Methods: The Matbench Test Set and Automatminer Reference Algorithm

direct_claims.text: Matbench v0.1 is a benchmark suite containing 13 supervised machine learning tasks (10 regression, 3 classification) for materials property prediction, with dataset sizes ranging from 312 to 132,752 samples.

Matbench contains data from 10 density functional theory-derived and experimental sources including Materials Project, Zhuo et al., Landolt-Bornstein Handbook, Castelli et al., JARVIS DFT 2D, and Citrine Informatics.
Matbench tasks include predicting optical, thermal, electronic, thermodynamic, tensile, and elastic properties given materials composition and/or crystal structure.

Automatminer is a fully-automated machine learning pipeline consisting of four stages (autofeaturization, cleaning, dimensionality reduction, and AutoML search) that requires no user intervention or hyperparameter tuning.

arti_00043.name: Virtual Node Graph Neural Network for Full Phonon Prediction

direct_claims.text: Virtual Node Graph Neural Network (VGNN) enables graph neural networks to handle variable output dimensions by incorporating virtual nodes that resemble phonon dynamical matrices.

Three virtual node approaches were developed: vector virtual nodes (VVN) outputting 3m Γ-phonon branches, matrix virtual nodes (MVN) with m² 3×3 matrices, and momentum-dependent matrix virtual nodes (k-MVN) for full band structure prediction.
VGNN achieves direct prediction of Γ-phonon spectra and full phonon dispersion using only atomic coordinates as input without prior knowledge of interatomic forces.
VGNN-based phonon calculation achieves significantly faster computation speed than ab initio methods (DFPT, frozen-phonon) while maintaining reasonable accuracy.

arti_00044.name: Evaluation of Foundational Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials for Migration Barrier Predictions

direct_claims.text: MACE-MP-0 achieves the lowest mean absolute error (0.310 eV) in migration barrier predictions across the entire Dataset-2 of 574 migration paths.
Orb-v3 achieves the lowest MAE (0.198 eV) when evaluated on non-outlier data points (excluding systems with absolute errors >1 eV).
Orb-v3 and SevenNet classify materials as good versus bad ionic conductors with accuracy greater than 82% using a 500 meV migration barrier threshold.
All MLIPs struggle with high migration barrier predictions, with only 3.7-20.7% achieving acceptable accuracy (<0.1 eV error) in the 1.31-2.50 eV range.

arti_00045.name: DeePMD-kit v2: A software package for Deep Potential models

direct_claims.text: DeePMD-kit is an open-source software package that facilitates molecular dynamics simulations using Deep Potential machine learning potentials for computational chemistry and materials science.
DeePMD-kit supports multiple atomic descriptor types including local frame, DeepPot-SE, attention-based, and hybrid descriptors.

The DeepPot-SE descriptor is continuous up to the second-order derivative in its domain, unlike the local frame descriptor which is not smooth at the cutoff radius and when exchanging the order of two nearest neighbors.
None of the tested descriptors outperforms the others in terms of accuracy across all datasets.

arti_00047.name: Challenges and opportunities for machine learning in multiscale computational modeling

direct_claims.text: Machine learning can serve as a surrogate for, accelerate, or augment traditional numerical methods in multiscale computational modeling.

ML-based simulation can achieve comparable fidelity to direct numerical simulation while being considerably faster in computation time, with convolutional neural networks producing high-fidelity estimation of materials microstructure response with multiple orders of magnitude faster computation.
Hierarchical multiscale modeling approaches require large amounts of memory and storage space to store precomputed quantities of interest.
Concurrent multiscale modeling approaches face formidable computation costs as the problem size increases.

arti_00048.name: Machine-learning based interatomic potential for amorphous carbon

direct_claims.text: The Gaussian approximation potential (GAP) enables atomistic simulations with close-to-DFT accuracy at computational costs many orders of magnitude lower than quantum-mechanical methods.

Combined two-body, three-body, and SOAP many-body descriptors are necessary for GAP to achieve the accuracy limit imposed by force locality and make physically meaningful predictions; models using only subsets of descriptors produce unphysical structures during molecular dynamics simulations.

GAP predicts diamond lattice parameter (3.539 Å) very close to DFT-LDA reference (3.532 Å), outperforming screened Tersoff potential (3.566 Å), with bulk modulus and elastic constants reasonably close to DFT reference values.
GAP radial and angular distribution functions for liquid and amorphous carbon closely match DFT reference results, including peak locations, extents, and overall curve shapes.

arti_00049.name: The AFLOW Standard for High-Throughput Materials Science Calculations

direct_claims.text: The AFLOW standard enables reproducible high-throughput DFT calculations through standardized parameter sets for k-point density, energy cut-offs, exchange-correlation functionals, pseudopotentials, DFT+U parameters, and convergence criteria.
The AFLOWLIB repository contains calculated properties of over 625,000 materials across Binary Alloy Project, Electronic Structure database, Heusler database, and Elements database.
AFLOW calculations follow a standardized sequential workflow: RELAX1 → RELAX2 → STATIC → BANDS for materials in the Elements, ICSD, and Heusler databases.

Default NKPPRA values for non-BANDS calculations vary by database: Binary Alloy uses 6000 for RELAX, Heusler uses 10000 for STATIC and 6000 for RELAX, and ICSD uses 10000 for STATIC and 8000 for RELAX.

arti_00050.name: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials: A Review and Framework for Understanding MLIPs

direct_claims.text: FastCHGNet trains in 1.5 hours using 32 GPUs compared to 8.3 days on a single A100 GPU for the original CHGNet model.
MLIPs map atomic configurations to total energy and provide forces and stresses as analytical derivatives of the potential energy surface.
MLIPs use highly flexible functional forms (e.g., neural networks) while PBPs use highly constrained forms guided by physical intuition (e.g., Lennard-Jones).
Approximately 40% of the UK's academic HPC was spent on DFT calculations in a recent year, most of which was AIMD.

arti_00051.name: Discovering Melting Temperature Prediction Models of Inorganic Solids by Combining Supervised and Unsupervised Learning

direct_claims.text: A curated dataset of 476 binary ionic compound melting temperatures spanning 0-4,000°C was compiled for machine learning model development.
The best one-step gradient-boosted tree regression model achieves 165±4 K MAE and 0.89 R² on the test set for melting temperature prediction.
A two-step approach combining unsupervised clustering with supervised regression achieves 156±4 K MAE and 0.92 R², outperforming direct one-step supervised learning.
Cluster 1 (198 compounds, mostly ionic halides and oxides) achieves 136±5 K MAE and 0.92 R², while Cluster 2 (222 compounds, mostly covalent carbides and nitrides) achieves 189±7 K MAE and 0.90 R².

arti_00052.name: Scaling deep learning for materials discovery

direct_claims.text: GNoME discovered 2.2 million crystal structures stable with respect to the Materials Project, with 381,000 newly on the convex hull, representing an order-of-magnitude expansion from all previous discoveries.
736 GNoME-discovered structures match experimentally validated ICSD structures, with 184 representing novel discoveries since the project began.

GNoME achieves hit rates above 80% for structural predictions and 33% for composition-only predictions, compared to 1% in previous work, with active learning improving from less than 6% and 3% respectively over six rounds.
Final GNoME models predict energies with a mean absolute error of 11 meV per atom on relaxed structures, improved from 21 meV per atom in the initial model trained on Materials Project data.

cite_00005.name: SchNet

direct_claims.text: SchNet provides rotationally invariant energy predictions and rotationally equivariant, energy‑conserving force predictions by defining forces as the negative gradient of the predicted energy.

When trained on MD17 trajectories with a combined energy‑and‑force loss, SchNet achieves energy MAE ≤0.12 kcal/mol and force MAE ≤0.33 kcal/mol/Å, matching or surpassing GDML and DTNN on all tested molecules, including flexible ones such as malonaldehyde and ethanol.
Training SchNet with forces on only 1,000 examples yields better accuracy than training on 50,000 examples using energies alone, demonstrating that force information improves data efficiency.

On the ISO17 benchmark, SchNet reaches chemical‑accuracy (≈0.5 kcal/mol MAE) for energy predictions on molecules seen during training and further improves predictions on unseen isomers when forces are included in training.

direct_claims.text: An E(3)‑equivariant graph neural network architecture guarantees rotational invariance of predicted phase‑averaged quantities.
Graph neural network architectures such as MEGNet and SchNet enhance prediction of phase transitions, defect dynamics, and bulk material properties relative to classical computational approaches.
The E(3)-equivariant graph neural network architecture automatically preserves crystalline symmetries, yielding the correct acoustic‑sum‑rule zero modes without additional corrections.
Virtual Node Graph Neural Network (VGNN) enables graph neural networks to handle variable output dimensions by incorporating virtual nodes that resemble phonon dynamical matrices.

cite_00018.name: Materials Project

direct_claims.text: The Materials Project database contains computed structural, electronic, and energetic data for over 33,000 inorganic compounds, generated using more than 15 million CPU‑hours of computation.
The Materials Project provides an open RESTful API and a high‑level Python library (pymatgen) that enable programmatic querying and analysis of the full dataset.

Visual warnings are displayed on the Materials Project website for compounds whose calculated oxidation states, cell volumes, or bond lengths deviate significantly from experimental norms, helping users assess data reliability.

Using Materials Project tools, researchers designed a new class of sodium‑based carbonophosphate compounds, predicted them to be thermodynamically stable, synthesized them hydrothermally, and experimentally confirmed their Li‑ion battery performance after ion exchange.

cite_00046.name: UMA

direct_claims.text: UMA models are trained on approximately 500 million unique 3D atomic structures (459M training examples with over 30 billion atoms) across five domains, representing the largest training runs to date for atomic models and covering nearly the entire chemical space except radioactive elements.
UMA sets new state-of-the-art performance on Matbench Discovery and AdsorbML benchmarks, with UMA-M achieving the highest F1 score to date (0.929) on Matbench Discovery.
UMA-M reduces OC20 S2EF adsorption energy prediction errors by approximately 80% compared to previous state-of-the-art models, achieving 33.4 meV MAE versus 149.1 meV for EquiformerV2-OC20.
UMA models conserve energy in NVE molecular dynamics simulations across all tested configurations spanning materials and molecules benchmarks.

cite_00048.name: MACE

direct_claims.text: Baseline versions of MACE and Allegro are degenerate with respect to total charge and cannot distinguish between molecules with different charge states without long-range corrections.

MACE without long-range correction does not generalize well to out-of-distribution samples, while integration of long-range correction schemes has significant effects on both MACE and Allegro architectures.
MACE-MP-0 achieves the lowest mean absolute error (0.310 eV) in migration barrier predictions across the entire Dataset-2 of 574 migration paths.
SevenNet exhibits the highest fraction of good local geometry predictions (0.719) while MACE-MP-0 exhibits the lowest fraction of bad geometry predictions (0.190) among all tested MLIPs.

cite_00049.name: NequIP

direct_claims.text: NequIP achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on the MD-17 benchmark, surpassing invariant GNN‑IPs, shallow neural networks, and kernel‑based methods.
NequIP outperforms kernel‑based approaches such as sGDML and FCHL19/GPR across benchmarks, including small-data regimes and the MD-17 dataset.
NequIP requires up to three orders of magnitude fewer training configurations than existing neural interatomic potentials to reach comparable accuracy.
When trained on only 133 structures (~1 k frames), NequIP outperforms DeepMD trained on 133,500 structures for liquid water and ice simulations.

The eSEN model achieves an F1 score of 0.925 and energy-above-hull MAE of 18 meV/atom when pretrained on OMat24, with eSEN and equiformerV2 models with DeNS outperforming their non-DeNS counterparts and all other third-party models in the Matbench Discovery benchmark task.

EquiformerV2+DeNS (a universal interatomic potential) achieves the highest classification performance among all evaluated models, with F1 scores up to 0.983, ROC AUC 0.96, and discovery acceleration factors up to 6.33, establishing state‑of‑the‑art for ML‑guided materials discovery.

Extrapolation performance degrades with increasing WBM batch number for most models, especially Wrenformer and Voronoi RF, while universal interatomic potential models (e.g., EquiformerV2, ORB) show minimal degradation across batches.

cite_00062.name: M3GNet

direct_claims.text: M3GNet and CHGNet exhibit systematic bias toward underestimating migration barriers, with 73.1% and 78.2% of predictions being underestimates respectively.
CHGNet and M3GNet demonstrate superior performance for materials with low migration barriers but lack consistency over wider barrier ranges.
M3GNet achieves test mean absolute errors of 35 meV/atom for energy, 72 meV/Angstrom for force, and 0.41 GPa for stress.
MACE-MP0 performed best for discovering new stable materials with classification F1 score of 0.67, followed by CHGNet (0.61) and M3GNet (0.57).

cite_00063.name: CHGNet

direct_claims.text: CHGNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Matbench Discovery benchmark, outperforming eight other submitted models.

On the Materials Project Trajectory test set, CHGNet trained with magnetic moment labels attains mean absolute errors of 30 meV/atom for energy, 77 meV/Å for forces, 0.348 GPa for stress, and 0.032 µB for magnetic moments.

CHGNet molecular dynamics simulations of Li superionic conductors reproduce room‑temperature ionic conductivities and activation energies within the error bars of AIMD, correctly distinguishing faster from slower conductors.
CHGNet integrates magnetic moment labels as a proxy for atomic charge, enabling inference of atomic charges and accurate differentiation of oxidation states such as V³⁺/V⁴⁺ and Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺.

direct_claims.text: TensorNet‑MatPES predicts ionic conductivities of Li/Na solid electrolytes with high fidelity (positive R²), whereas TensorNet‑MPF severely overestimates conductivities and yields a negative R².

direct_claims.text: EquiformerV2 can scale Lmax to 6 or 8 on OC20 dataset using eSCN convolutions that reduce computational cost from O(L^6) to O(L^3), whereas original Equiformer is impractical for Lmax > 2 on large-scale datasets.

EquiformerV2 offers better speed-accuracy trade-offs than Equiformer, being 2.3x faster at Lmax=2 while achieving better force MAE, and requiring 1.4x less training time when increasing Lmax from 2 to 4.
EquiformerV2 achieves better results than Equiformer on 9 out of 12 tasks on the QM9 dataset and is the overall best performing model.

cite_00110.name: DTNN

direct_claims.text: When trained on MD17 trajectories with a combined energy‑and‑force loss, SchNet achieves energy MAE ≤0.12 kcal/mol and force MAE ≤0.33 kcal/mol/Å, matching or surpassing GDML and DTNN on all tested molecules, including flexible ones such as malonaldehyde and ethanol.
On the QM9 benchmark, SchNet attains a mean absolute error of 0.31 kcal/mol for total‑energy prediction with 110 k training examples, outperforming DTNN (0.84) and enn‑s2s (0.45).

The Message Passing Neural Network (MPNN) achieves state‑of‑the‑art performance on all QM9 regression targets, reaching chemical accuracy on 11 of the 13 targets and outperforming prior models such as SchNet and DTNN.

For internal energy at 0 K (U0), enthalpy (H), Gibbs free energy (G), heat capacity at constant volume (Cv), and highest vibrational frequency (Ω), the MPNN records lower mean absolute errors than SchNet and DTNN (U0 MAE 0.45 vs 0.55/0.72; H 0.39 vs 0.59/0.80; G 0.44 vs 0.55/0.74; Cv 0.80 vs 0.99/1.71; Ω 0.19 vs 0.41/0.78).

cite_00148.name: Gaussian quadrature

direct_claims.text: Standard Gaussian quadrature rules produce frame‑dependent (non‑objective) phase‑averaged internal energies for rotated crystal lattices.
Gaussian quadrature leads to abrupt energy jumps and fictitious minima when neighbor cut‑off radii change during large deformations.
Third‑order Gaussian quadrature fails to approximate phase‑space integrals for bulk aluminum above 300 K, producing spurious minima in the Helmholtz free‑energy landscape.
Fifth‑order Gaussian quadrature yields internal energies and free‑energy curves that remain in good agreement with molecular dynamics results across the full temperature range studied.

cite_00180.name: MLIP

direct_claims.text: LiFlow achieves speed‑ups of up to ~600,000× over ab initio molecular dynamics (and ~400× over MLIP), predicting a 1 ns trajectory in 48 s for a 2 × 2 × 1 LGPS supercell and 352 s for a 4 × 4 × 4 supercell.

Non-conservative (unconstrained) MLIP models consistently show 2-3× theoretical speed-up over their conservative counterparts, with direct force prediction providing additional 2-3× speedup compared to forces computed via automatic differentiation.

Elastic moduli predictions are very sensitive to the lack of energy conservation in MLIP models, and non-conservative models consistently perform worse on matbench-discovery downstream tasks despite achieving better training and validation accuracies.

DFT setting inconsistency between training and evaluation datasets significantly affects MLIP model performance comparisons, with PET-OMAD performing worse than PET-OAM and PET-MPtrj on Inorganic Materials due to differences in ab initio theory levels.

cite_00191.name: GAP

direct_claims.text: Including electronic entropy via charge‑decorated cluster expansions, CHGNet reproduces the experimentally observed miscibility gap and eutectoid‑like transition in the LiₓFePO₄ phase diagram, whereas a non‑charge‑decorated model fails to capture these features.
For the disordered solid‑electrolyte Li10Si1.5P1.5S11.5Cl0.5, the universal model predicts an insulating behavior with a band gap of 1.4 eV.

High‑throughput screening of 188,722 GeNOME crystals with the universal model identifies 21,973 insulators (3,940 direct‑gap) and 5,109 flat‑band materials, nearly doubling the entries in the Materials Flatband Database.

The Gaussian Approximation Potential (GAP) for silicon reproduces density functional theory reference results across a wide range of observable properties, including bulk crystal, liquid, amorphous phases, and point, line, and plane defects.

EFA enables modeling of long-range interactions without requiring explicit neighbor cutoffs and outperforms CELLI on most benchmarking subsplits when reference charges are unavailable.

Total charge embeddings can recover much of CELLI's performance on some datasets but generalize poorly in size-based extrapolation and should be viewed as a potential extension rather than replacement for long-range methods.
EFA and CELLI do not lead to improvements when no reference charges are provided in the ODAC25 dataset.

cite_00200.name: SOAP

direct_claims.text: Combining a simple repulsive pair potential with a many‑body SOAP‑kernel term in the GAP framework yields meV‑per‑atom accuracy for silicon energetics.
The Smooth Overlap of Atomic Positions (SOAP) kernel captures the regularity of the silicon potential energy surface, leading to accurate interpolation within the sampled configuration space.

Combined two-body, three-body, and SOAP many-body descriptors are necessary for GAP to achieve the accuracy limit imposed by force locality and make physically meaningful predictions; models using only subsets of descriptors produce unphysical structures during molecular dynamics simulations.

direct_claims.text: The atomic cluster expansion (ACE) is generalized to model scalar, vectorial and tensorial atomic properties and to include additional atomic degrees of freedom—species, magnetic moments, and charges—on equal footing with atomic positions.

Moments Tensor Potentials (MTP) and the Spectral Neighbor Analysis Potential (SNAP) can be expressed exactly as special cases of the ACE.

cite_00254.name: DeepH

direct_claims.text: DeepH predicts DFT Hamiltonian matrix elements for graphene with an average mean absolute error of 2.1 meV and a coefficient of determination r² = 0.9994 across all orbital combinations.
When applied to unseen graphene configurations sampled between 100 K and 400 K, DeepH maintains a mean absolute error of 1.9 meV for Hamiltonian matrix elements.
For monolayer MoS₂, DeepH predicts DFT Hamiltonian matrix elements with average mean absolute errors of 1.3 meV (Mo–Mo), 1.0 meV (Mo–S), 0.7 meV (S–Mo), and 0.8 meV (S–S).
Band structures and electric susceptibility computed from DeepH for MoS₂ match DFT results closely.

cite_00255.name: DeepH‑E3

direct_claims.text: DeepH‑E3 reproduces the band structure of magic‑angle twisted bilayer graphene (θ = 1.08°, 11 164 atoms) in excellent agreement with DFT and low‑energy continuum models, correctly capturing the flat bands near the Fermi level.

DeepH‑E3 predicts a spin‑orbit‑coupling‑induced topological quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer Bi₂Te₃, evidenced by band‑gap closing and reopening and a change of the Z₂ invariant from 0 to 1 as SOC strength increases.
DeepH‑E3 attains sub‑meV accuracy after training on only a few hundred DFT calculations of small, non‑twisted structures, demonstrating high data efficiency.
DeepH‑E3 generalizes across diverse material systems—including graphene, MoS₂, bismuthene, Bi₂Se₃, and Bi₂Te₃—achieving consistently sub‑meV Hamiltonian prediction errors.

cite_00273.name: PBE

direct_claims.text: The MatPES v2025.1 dataset contains 504,811 structures (434,712 PBE and 387,897 r2SCAN calculations) sampled from a configuration space of ~281 million MD snapshots and ~16 billion atomic environments.
The r2SCAN functional provides a more accurate description of interatomic bonding than PBE, leading to improved potential‑energy‑surface quality in the MatPES r2SCAN dataset.

Compared with MPRelax and OMat24, the MatPES PBE dataset exhibits a more Gaussian‑like distribution of cohesive energies per atom and a log‑normal‑like distribution of force magnitudes, indicating a better balance of on‑ and off‑equilibrium structures.

Training a TensorNet model on the 400 k‑structure MatPES‑PBE dataset requires approximately 15 minutes per epoch on a single RTX A6000 GPU, whereas training on the 100 M‑structure OMat24 dataset needs about 20 hours per epoch on sixteen A100 GPUs, highlighting the computational efficiency of MatPES.

cite_00274.name: AFLOW

direct_claims.text: The AFLOW standard enables reproducible high-throughput DFT calculations through standardized parameter sets for k-point density, energy cut-offs, exchange-correlation functionals, pseudopotentials, DFT+U parameters, and convergence criteria.
AFLOW calculations follow a standardized sequential workflow: RELAX1 → RELAX2 → STATIC → BANDS for materials in the Elements, ICSD, and Heusler databases.

Following the AFLOW standard enables materials science researchers to reproduce AFLOWLIB consortium results and make direct comparisons of properties between different materials for identifying trends and formulating design rules.
AFLOW can automatically calculate a wide suite of physical observables across a large database of structures with minimal human intervention.

cite_00279.name: DFT+U

direct_claims.text: The AFLOW standard enables reproducible high-throughput DFT calculations through standardized parameter sets for k-point density, energy cut-offs, exchange-correlation functionals, pseudopotentials, DFT+U parameters, and convergence criteria.
DFT+U corrections are applied to the entire ICSD database and certain Heusler database entries containing O, S, Se, and F elements, but not to the Binary Alloy database.

Specific Ueff parameters are defined for d-block elements (Table 4) and U, J parameters for f-block elements (Table 5) to correct self-interaction error in DFT+U calculations, with values ranging from 1.9 eV (In) to 7.5 eV (Zn).

A Hubbard U parameter of 2.5 eV in DFT+U (with a vdW‑DF exchange‑correlation functional) reproduces the experimental average lithiation voltages of LiCoO₂ across the composition ranges {0‑1}, {0‑0.5}, and {0.5‑1}.

cite_00311.name: OMat24

direct_claims.text: Fine-tuning models pre-trained on OMat24 to the MAD dataset achieves near-converged validation metrics in 30-100 epochs versus 700+ epochs when training from scratch, halving validation energy and force errors and achieving 50% lower test error than training on MAD alone.
UMLIPs trained on the MatPES dataset achieve test mean absolute errors in energies that are 4–10 times lower than UMLIPs trained on the larger MPRelax or OMat24 datasets.

Across equilibrium, near‑equilibrium, and molecular‑dynamics property benchmarks, MatPES‑trained UMLIPs match or surpass the performance of models trained on much larger datasets such as OMat24 (≈100 M structures).
Molecular‑dynamics simulations using MatPES‑trained UMLIPs exhibit markedly higher stability, with median termination temperatures up to ~1,900 K, versus ~1,300–1,500 K for MPRelax and OMat24 models.

cite_00354.name: CGCNN

direct_claims.text: CGCNN classifies metals versus semiconductors with an area under the ROC curve of 0.95 and an overall accuracy of 0.90.

When applied to a set of 1,585 crystals with elastic properties, CGCNN predicts bulk modulus with a mean absolute error of 0.077 log(GPa) and shear modulus with a mean absolute error of 0.114 log(GPa), demonstrating good generalization.
Using roughly 10⁴ training examples, CGCNN attains DFT‑level accuracy for eight distinct material properties across diverse crystal types and compositions.

Compared with a prior statistical‑learning approach, CGCNN achieves similar or lower root‑mean‑square errors for bulk modulus (0.075 log(GPa) vs 0.105) and shear modulus (0.127 log(GPa) vs 0.138) using the same training data.

direct_claims.text: CHGNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Matbench Discovery benchmark, outperforming eight other submitted models.

The PET model achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on matbench-discovery benchmark (DAF=6.075, Accuracy=0.977, F1=0.924) and exceeds SOTA on SPICE molecular benchmark across most subsets for both energy and force predictions.

Elastic moduli predictions are very sensitive to the lack of energy conservation in MLIP models, and non-conservative models consistently perform worse on matbench-discovery downstream tasks despite achieving better training and validation accuracies.

cite_00370.name: OQMD

direct_claims.text: The Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD) contains over 200,000 DFT‑calculated crystal structures, including experimental ICSD entries and theoretical prototype structures, and is freely accessible to the scientific community without usage restrictions.
At 0 K and zero pressure, 23 % of the 32,489 ICSD structures in the OQMD are thermodynamically stable according to grand canonical linear programming analysis.
The average error between DFT‑predicted formation energies in the OQMD and experimental values from the SGTE database is 24 meV/atom, with a mean absolute error of 113 meV/atom.
All eleven experimentally known rare‑earth‑containing Mg‑XL‑XS LPSO systems are correctly predicted to be thermodynamically stable by DFT calculations using OQMD convex hulls.

cite_00374.name: OC20

direct_claims.text: EquiformerV2 outperforms state-of-the-art methods on OC20 and OC22 datasets, improving upon eSCN by 4-9% on force MAE and 4-18.9% on energy MAE.
EquiformerV2 trained on only OC22 (8.4M structures) achieves better results than GemNet-OC trained on both OC20 (130M structures) and OC22, demonstrating significantly better data efficiency.

EquiformerV2 can scale Lmax to 6 or 8 on OC20 dataset using eSCN convolutions that reduce computational cost from O(L^6) to O(L^3), whereas original Equiformer is impractical for Lmax > 2 on large-scale datasets.
UMA-M reduces OC20 S2EF adsorption energy prediction errors by approximately 80% compared to previous state-of-the-art models, achieving 33.4 meV MAE versus 149.1 meV for EquiformerV2-OC20.

cite_00375.name: MatPES

direct_claims.text: UMLIPs trained on the MatPES dataset achieve test mean absolute errors in energies that are 4–10 times lower than UMLIPs trained on the larger MPRelax or OMat24 datasets.

Across equilibrium, near‑equilibrium, and molecular‑dynamics property benchmarks, MatPES‑trained UMLIPs match or surpass the performance of models trained on much larger datasets such as OMat24 (≈100 M structures).
Molecular‑dynamics simulations using MatPES‑trained UMLIPs exhibit markedly higher stability, with median termination temperatures up to ~1,900 K, versus ~1,300–1,500 K for MPRelax and OMat24 models.

On near‑equilibrium benchmarks, MatPES UMLIPs significantly improve the prediction of shear modulus (G_VRH) and off‑equilibrium forces while achieving similar bulk‑modulus (K_VRH) and heat‑capacity (C_V) accuracy compared to MPRelax and OMat24 models.

cite_00376.name: WBM

direct_claims.text: The WBM test split consistently yields the highest prediction errors, suggesting it represents the most important distribution shift for model generalization testing.

The WBM test set contains 215,488 unique prototype structures (32,942 thermodynamically stable), is enriched in actinides, lanthanides, metalloids and noble‑transition metals while under‑representing oxygen, is dominated by ternary phases (~75 %), and most structures have fewer than 100 atomic sites, contrasting with the Materials Project training distribution.

Extrapolation performance degrades with increasing WBM batch number for most models, especially Wrenformer and Voronoi RF, while universal interatomic potential models (e.g., EquiformerV2, ORB) show minimal degradation across batches.

direct_claims.text: The AFLOWLIB repository contains calculated properties of over 625,000 materials across Binary Alloy Project, Electronic Structure database, Heusler database, and Elements database.

Following the AFLOW standard enables materials science researchers to reproduce AFLOWLIB consortium results and make direct comparisons of properties between different materials for identifying trends and formulating design rules.
The AFLOWLIB data is accessible through a REST-API for standardized data exchange.

direct_claims.text: The Message Passing Neural Network (MPNN) achieves state‑of‑the‑art performance on all QM9 regression targets, reaching chemical accuracy on 11 of the 13 targets and outperforming prior models such as SchNet and DTNN.
Inference with the MPNN takes roughly 10⁻² seconds per molecule, about 300,000 times faster than the DFT reference calculation (~10³ seconds).
Learning directly from molecular graphs without handcrafted descriptors enables the MPNN to achieve lower prediction errors than descriptor‑based methods.
Across all QM9 properties, the MPNN reduces the mean absolute error by 30–70 % relative to the best previously reported graph‑neural‑network baseline.

comp_00151.name: eSCN convolutions

direct_claims.text: EquiformerV2 can scale Lmax to 6 or 8 on OC20 dataset using eSCN convolutions that reduce computational cost from O(L^6) to O(L^3), whereas original Equiformer is impractical for Lmax > 2 on large-scale datasets.

EquiformerV2 incorporates three architectural improvements: attention re-normalization, separable S2 activation, and separable layer normalization, replacing SO(3) convolutions with eSCN convolutions to efficiently incorporate higher-degree tensors.
eSCN convolutions reduce SO(3) tensor product complexity by replacing non-trivial paths with SO(2) linear operations while maintaining equivariance.

comp_00220.name: Uncertainty quantification

direct_claims.text: Beyond‑DFT methods (HSE06, PBE0, G0W0, DMFT) are generated for a subset of materials to provide higher‑level reference data and enable uncertainty quantification.
The Gaussian process regression framework underlying GAP provides an uncertainty quantification that qualitatively estimates the potential’s accuracy for any given atomic configuration.

Uncertainty quantification based on latent‑space Euclidean distance provides error estimates that correlate with prediction errors, allowing exclusion of transitions whose uncertainty exceeds 50 % of the absolute free‑energy difference.

comp_00273.name: D4FT

direct_claims.text: The QR‑based reparameterization used in D4FT preserves the orthonormal constraints of Kohn‑Sham orbitals, making the search space equivalent to the original orthogonal function space, as proved in Proposition 3.1, and can be interpreted as projected gradient descent on the orthogonal constraint set.

Direct minimization of the total KS‑DFT energy with stochastic gradient descent reduces the asymptotic computational complexity from O(N⁴) to O(N³), and the full‑batch D4FT algorithm has complexity O(nN²)+O(n²N²), which is lower than the O(n²N²) complexity of conventional SCF; minibatch training further lowers the cost.
D4FT converges to a self‑consistent Kohn‑Sham solution that satisfies the eigenfunction condition.
Across a benchmark set ranging from He to benzene, D4FT reproduces ground‑state energies of the reference PySCF implementation with deviations ≤0.02 Ha (LSDA/6‑31g and LSDA/STO‑3g).

comp_00400.name: OMat24 dataset

direct_claims.text: Training a TensorNet model on the 400 k‑structure MatPES‑PBE dataset requires approximately 15 minutes per epoch on a single RTX A6000 GPU, whereas training on the 100 M‑structure OMat24 dataset needs about 20 hours per epoch on sixteen A100 GPUs, highlighting the computational efficiency of MatPES.

The diversity of the larger OMat24 dataset does not benefit from the regularization or augmentation provided by DeNS, whereas dataset augmentation techniques like DeNS can significantly enhance performance when training solely on the MPtraj dataset.
Rattled systems in the OMat24 dataset have deleterious effects on model performance when evaluated on out-of-distribution hetero-diatomic systems.

comp_00447.name: Automatminer

direct_claims.text: Automatminer is a fully-automated machine learning pipeline consisting of four stages (autofeaturization, cleaning, dimensionality reduction, and AutoML search) that requires no user intervention or hyperparameter tuning.
Automatminer Express preset achieves the best performance on 8 of 13 tasks in the Matbench benchmark.
Automatminer's auto-generated models outperform or equal the Random Forest model across all Matbench tasks except predicting formation energies across the Materials Project.

Descriptor-based Automatminer and RF models have lower errors on small datasets but their improvement rates are shallower, with AutoML's advantage over conventional techniques narrowing as sample count increases and essentially lost near 10^5 samples.

comp_00448.name: Matbench

direct_claims.text: CHGNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Matbench Discovery benchmark, outperforming eight other submitted models.

The PET model achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on matbench-discovery benchmark (DAF=6.075, Accuracy=0.977, F1=0.924) and exceeds SOTA on SPICE molecular benchmark across most subsets for both energy and force predictions.
Conservative PET-OAM models achieve state-of-the-art performance on phonon tasks in matbench-discovery and the best overall accuracy in predicting shear modulus among tested models.

Elastic moduli predictions are very sensitive to the lack of energy conservation in MLIP models, and non-conservative models consistently perform worse on matbench-discovery downstream tasks despite achieving better training and validation accuracies.

comp_00481.name: CHGNet

direct_claims.text: CHGNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Matbench Discovery benchmark, outperforming eight other submitted models.

On the Materials Project Trajectory test set, CHGNet trained with magnetic moment labels attains mean absolute errors of 30 meV/atom for energy, 77 meV/Å for forces, 0.348 GPa for stress, and 0.032 µB for magnetic moments.

CHGNet molecular dynamics simulations of Li superionic conductors reproduce room‑temperature ionic conductivities and activation energies within the error bars of AIMD, correctly distinguishing faster from slower conductors.
CHGNet integrates magnetic moment labels as a proxy for atomic charge, enabling inference of atomic charges and accurate differentiation of oxidation states such as V³⁺/V⁴⁺ and Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺.

direct_claims.text: M3GNet and CHGNet exhibit systematic bias toward underestimating migration barriers, with 73.1% and 78.2% of predictions being underestimates respectively.
CHGNet and M3GNet demonstrate superior performance for materials with low migration barriers but lack consistency over wider barrier ranges.
M3GNet achieves test mean absolute errors of 35 meV/atom for energy, 72 meV/Angstrom for force, and 0.41 GPa for stress.
MACE-MP0 performed best for discovering new stable materials with classification F1 score of 0.67, followed by CHGNet (0.61) and M3GNet (0.57).

direct_claims.text: GNoME was trained on an in-house database of roughly 80 million DFT calculations.
GNoME discovered over 2.2 million new stable inorganic materials and more than 45 000 new crystal prototypes, an order‑of‑magnitude increase over prior discovery efforts.
Architecture modifications reduced SevenNet-0 total model parameters from 16.24 million (GNoME) to 0.84 million.

GNoME discovered 2.2 million crystal structures stable with respect to the Materials Project, with 381,000 newly on the convex hull, representing an order-of-magnitude expansion from all previous discoveries.

comp_00692.name: CELLI

direct_claims.text: CELLI-based models trained with reference charges consistently produce physically meaningful results and exhibit good performance across biased split benchmarks on MOF datasets.
EFA enables modeling of long-range interactions without requiring explicit neighbor cutoffs and outperforms CELLI on most benchmarking subsplits when reference charges are unavailable.

Total charge embeddings can recover much of CELLI's performance on some datasets but generalize poorly in size-based extrapolation and should be viewed as a potential extension rather than replacement for long-range methods.
EFA and CELLI do not lead to improvements when no reference charges are provided in the ODAC25 dataset.

comp_00722.name: conservative models

direct_claims.text: Non-conservative models allow residual asymmetries to drive relaxation toward more stable close-packed structures, unlike equivariant models that remain trapped in symmetric but unstable configurations, though 70% (16%) of final configurations retain symmetry of initial structure with 0.01 Å threshold for conservative (non-conservative) models.

Elastic moduli predictions are very sensitive to the lack of energy conservation in MLIP models, and non-conservative models consistently perform worse on matbench-discovery downstream tasks despite achieving better training and validation accuracies.

A two-step training strategy with direct force pretraining followed by conservative finetuning results in eSEN models with higher accuracy requiring less total training epochs and time compared to training conservative models from scratch.
Orb-v3-direct-20 uses only 32.8GB GPU memory for 100,000 atom systems and completes in under half a second, while all baseline methods and conservative models encounter Out Of Memory errors.

direct_claims.text: UMA sets new state-of-the-art performance on Matbench Discovery and AdsorbML benchmarks, with UMA-M achieving the highest F1 score to date (0.929) on Matbench Discovery.
UMA-M reduces OC20 S2EF adsorption energy prediction errors by approximately 80% compared to previous state-of-the-art models, achieving 33.4 meV MAE versus 149.1 meV for EquiformerV2-OC20.
UMA-M achieves ligand strain errors approaching DFT reference accuracy, demonstrating practical surrogate capability for structure-based drug design applications.

meth_00037.name: M3GNet

direct_claims.text: The final M3GNet interatomic potential achieves test mean absolute errors of 0.035 eV/atom for energy, 0.072 eV/Å for forces, and 0.41 GPa for stresses on a held‑out Materials Project dataset covering 89 elements.
Relaxing test crystals with M3GNet reduces median volume error from 2.4 % to 0.6 % and energy mean absolute error from 0.169 eV/atom to 0.035 eV/atom relative to DFT‑relaxed references.

A single‑CPU M3GNet relaxation completes in about 22 seconds, compared with 15 hours on 32 cores for DFT; pre‑relaxation with M3GNet shortens subsequent DFT relaxation time by roughly a factor of three and reduces total CPU time by an average factor of 2.97.

Screening 31.7 million hypothetical crystals with M3GNet identifies approximately 1.8 million candidates with predicted hull distances below 0.001 eV/atom, and among the 2,000 lowest‑energy candidates, 1,578 are confirmed stable (Ehull < 0.001 eV/atom) by DFT.

meth_00038.name: CHGNet

direct_claims.text: CHGNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Matbench Discovery benchmark, outperforming eight other submitted models.

On the Materials Project Trajectory test set, CHGNet trained with magnetic moment labels attains mean absolute errors of 30 meV/atom for energy, 77 meV/Å for forces, 0.348 GPa for stress, and 0.032 µB for magnetic moments.

CHGNet molecular dynamics simulations of Li superionic conductors reproduce room‑temperature ionic conductivities and activation energies within the error bars of AIMD, correctly distinguishing faster from slower conductors.
CHGNet integrates magnetic moment labels as a proxy for atomic charge, enabling inference of atomic charges and accurate differentiation of oxidation states such as V³⁺/V⁴⁺ and Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺.
